title: Superconductivity in High-Entropy Alloy System Containing Tb.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: a multicomponent high-entropy alloy precursor made of elements such as Tb, Nb, Zr, Hf, and Ti powders
recollection.intervention: Guess: arc melting or spark-plasma sintering followed by rapid quenching to form a single-phase solid solution; possibly pressure-assisted annealing to tune disorder
recollection.structure: Guess: a body-centered-cubic (BCC) solid-solution high-entropy alloy with nanoscale chemical disorder but no long-range ordering
recollection.mechanism: Guess: superconductivity arising from strong electron–phonon coupling in the disordered BCC lattice, with magnetic Tb diluted enough that Kondo screening or pair breaking is minimized
recollection.results: Guess: superconducting transition temperature Tc ≈ 6–8 K at ambient pressure, upper critical field μ0Hc2(0) ≈ 5–6 T, and moderate residual-resistivity ratio (~1.5) indicating high disorder

score.note: The recollection correctly guesses arc melting and a BCC alloy matrix, but incorrectly suggests a single-phase material and adds unsupported processing. It misses the Tb/Tb2O3 secondary phases and the observed degradation of superconductivity. The proposed mechanism conflicts with the paper. The Hc2 estimate is near the measured 6.1 T, but the Tc estimate of 6–8 K is substantially above the actual 4.6–4.7 K.
